text:
Oliver: Heads-up — onboarding eosica/eosica-6b (Eosica6b) finished conversion to int4. Quick smoke shows generation perplexity jump and token alignment differences vs fp16.
Maria: Can you paste the smoke eval numbers? which quant backend? :thinking:
Oliver: Using our int4 pipeline (per-layer FP32->INT4 symmetric, kernel shim v2). Quick comparison on small eval set:
Aj: ```
MODEL	PPL_FP16	PPL_INT4	DELTA
Eosica6b_fp16	12.4	-
Eosica6b_int4	-	18.9	+6.5
``` 
Oliver: Also seeing token-level diffs at early timesteps; repeats and shifted alignment for words with uppercase letters.
Yuki: Hmm uppercase tokenization drift could be vocab normalization mismatch. Did we normalize casing before tokenization on fp16 vs conversion pipeline?
Oliver: We run the same tokenizer files but conversion script re-mapped token ids (we used a naive cast). suspect two things: rotary head-scale mismatch + token id remap around ASCII range for capitals.
Tim: Any logs for kv-cache token ids? small dump pls.
Oliver: ```
# kv cache token ids (fp16 vs int4) sample
fp16: [  45, 1023, 11,  67,  78,  300]
int4: [  45, 1023, 11,  68,  78,  300]
# note: 67 -> 68 at index 4 (capital letter 'C' -> 'D' example)
``` 
Maria: That single off-by-one smells like an endianness/byte-order or tokenizer normalization bug during conversion. But the delta in PPL is big — rotary scaling could amplify small id shifts.
Aj: I ran a quick ablation: revert rotary scale multiplier to fp16 baseline (force headwise scale=1.0) and run tiny decode (1000 tokens). PPL drops to 14.1. So rotary head-scale mismatch explains ~2.5 PPL.
Yuki: Nice repro. So two root causes: (1) token id remap around capitalization (off-by-one), (2) rotary head-scale differences post-quant. Fix both and re-eval.
Oliver: Plan: 1) run vocab roundtrip check tool to detect id mismatches across conversion (script attached) 2) force rotary headwise scale back to baseline in runtime as a temporary patch 3) re-run int4 smoke and full eval.
Tim: Can you drop the conversion snippet here? I'll add a lint check in the conversion pipeline.
Oliver: ```bash
# conversion excerpt
python convert_model.py --input hf/eosica-6b --out ./dump_int4 \
  --tokenizer-file tokenizers/eosica.json \# we noticed we accidentally used an older tokenizer copy
``` 
Maria: Also add a unit test: tokenize(normalize_case=True, text) should equal tokenize(fp16_tokenizer, text) across a sample set.
ci-bot: conversion-lint failed on last run: missing tokenizer checksum, flagged by #conv-lint. See: https://ci.internal/conv/8421 :warning:
Aj: After patching tokenizer mapping (fixed remap table) + enforcing fp16 rotary scaling on int4 runtime, quick eval:
Aj: ```
MODEL	PPL_FP16	PPL_INT4_FIXED	DELTA
Eosica6b_fp16	12.4	-
Eosica6b_int4_fixed	12.9	+0.5
``` 
Yuki: That's acceptable for now. Remaining 0.5 PPL could be quant noise.
Oliver: Will open PR with two commits: (A) conversion checksum and vocab-roundtrip test, (B) runtime opt to prefer fp16 rotary head scale from metadata when present. Marking canary for dedicated pool.
Tim: Add a monitor for per-token repeat rate for first 16 tokens after rollout, and a rollback trigger if repeat_rate > 0.02.
Maria: Can we add a small eval suite focusing on casing-sensitive prompts? I'll produce a 200-prompt set.
Oliver: Thanks — assigning tasks: Maria: casing prompts, Aj: patch conversion remap and report, Yuki: runtime patch, Tim: rollout monitor, I'll coordinate canary. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: Created issue RED-ML-1217 and canary task RED-OPS-334.
Oliver: Moving to PR stage, will post link when ready.
Tim: lgtm on plan — ping when PR is up and I'll schedule canary window.
